# The input contract

Trajectory inference tools describe a trajectory in different ways:
slingshot fits one principal curve per lineage and gives every cell a
pseudotime and a weight on each lineage [@street2018], Monocle3 learns a
principal graph and gives every cell one pseudotime from a root node
[@cao2019], and tradeSeq takes such weights to fit its own models
[@vandenberge2020]. scMaSigPro needs much less: for every cell,

* one **pseudotime** value, a number that orders the cells of a path, and
* one **path** label, the path that the cell belongs to.

Every cell has one path label: scMaSigPro uses hard assignments. When the
paths of a trajectory share their first cells, as the branches of a tree
share its trunk, those cells get labels of their own:

* the cells on every path get the **root** label;
* the cells on some of the paths but not all of them get a **link** label,
    the names of those paths joined by a separator, `_links_` by default;
* every other cell gets the name of its path, an **end** path.

`sc.restruct()` uses these labels to add the bins of the root and of the
links to the end paths that share them; the
[Shared root](https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/shared-root.html)
vignette shows how.

The two columns enter scMaSigPro in one of two ways:

* `as_scmp()` takes a `SingleCellExperiment` whose `colData()` holds them;
* `create_scmp()` takes a count matrix, genes by cells, and a data frame
    with one row per cell, named by cell, that holds them.

The rest of this vignette builds this table from the output of trajectory
tools. The bundled data set `multi.lin.sce` serves as the example: a
simulated trajectory with three end points [@vandenberge2020; @saelens2019],
whose cells Monocle3 placed on three paths that share a root and a link.

```{r load-data, message = FALSE}
library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("multi.lin.sce", package = "scMaSigPro")
table(colData(multi.lin.sce)$group)
```

# From lineage weights

`assign_paths()` turns lineage weights into path labels. It takes a matrix
of weights, one row per cell and one column per lineage, and the pseudotime
of each cell, either as a matrix of the same shape (one pseudotime per
lineage, as slingshot gives it) or as one vector (one pseudotime shared by
every lineage, as Monocle3 gives it). A cell is on a lineage when its weight
there is at least `min_weight`, 0.5 by default, and its pseudotime there is
known.

A small example with three lineages shows the rules:

```{r toy-weights}
weights <- rbind(
    cell1 = c(A = 1, B = 1, C = 1),
    cell2 = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8, C = 0.1),
    cell3 = c(A = 1, B = 0, C = 0),
    cell4 = c(A = 0, B = 0, C = 0.7),
    cell5 = c(A = 0.2, B = 0.3, C = 0.1)
)
pseudotime <- rbind(
    cell1 = c(A = 1, B = 1.2, C = 0.8),
    cell2 = c(A = 4, B = 5, C = NA),
    cell3 = c(A = 9, B = NA, C = NA),
    cell4 = c(A = NA, B = NA, C = 7),
    cell5 = c(A = 2, B = 2, C = 2)
)
assign_paths(pseudotime, weights)
```

`cell1` is on every lineage and becomes a root cell; `cell2` is on `A` and
`B` only and gets the link label `A_links_B`; `cell3` and `cell4` are on one
lineage each. A cell on several lineages gets the mean of its pseudotimes
there. `cell5` is on no lineage and is left out, with a message.

The weights are compared with `min_weight` as they are given. slingshot's
curve weights are close to 1 on every lineage for the cells of the root; for
weights that add up to 1 in each cell, a `min_weight` below 1 divided by the
number of lineages keeps the root cells.

# From slingshot

slingshot needs a low-dimensional embedding and clusters of cells. Here the
embedding is the t-SNE of `multi.lin.sce` and the clusters are its Monocle3
path labels, with the root as the start and the three end paths as the end
clusters. This section runs when slingshot is installed.

```{r slingshot}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("slingshot", quietly = TRUE)
leaves <- c("path_Y_15", "path_Y_18", "path_Y_52")
sds <- slingshot::slingshot(
    reducedDim(multi.lin.sce, "TSNE"),
    clusterLabels = colData(multi.lin.sce)$group,
    start.clus = "root",
    end.clus = leaves
)
slingshot::slingLineages(sds)
```

Each lineage ends in one of the end clusters, which gives it its name:

```{r slingshot-paths}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("slingshot", quietly = TRUE)
ends <- vapply(
    slingshot::slingLineages(sds), function(l) l[length(l)], character(1)
)
time <- slingshot::slingPseudotime(sds)
weights <- slingshot::slingCurveWeights(sds)
colnames(time) <- colnames(weights) <- ends

cells <- assign_paths(time, weights)
table(cells$Path)
```

The two tools draw the borders between the root, the link and the end
paths in different places; slingshot, for one, puts fewer cells in the root
than Monocle3 does here. Soft weights also place a few cells on two
lineages that share nothing but the root, here `path_Y_52` and one of the
other two; their labels look like links, but no segment of the trajectory
joins those paths. They are so few that the simplest choice is to leave
them out:

```{r slingshot-links}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("slingshot", quietly = TRUE)
link <- "path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18"
cells <- cells[cells$Path %in% c("root", link, leaves), ]
table(
    slingshot = cells$Path,
    monocle3 = colData(multi.lin.sce)[rownames(cells), "group"]
)
```

The cell table goes to `create_scmp()` with the counts of its cells. The
workflow then runs as for any other input; here on the first 100 genes, with
the root and the link added to the end paths by `sc.restruct()`:

```{r slingshot-workflow, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("slingshot", quietly = TRUE)
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Tile plot of the bins of the three end paths, each starting with the bins
#|   of the root.
genes <- rownames(multi.lin.sce)[seq_len(100)]
scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(multi.lin.sce)[genes, rownames(cells)],
    cell_data = cells,
    ptime_col = "Pseudotime",
    path_col = "Path"
)
scmp_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
scmp_ob <- sc.restruct(scmp_ob,
    end_node_list = as.list(leaves),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list(link),
    verbose = FALSE
)
plotBinTile(scmp_ob)
scmp_ob <- sc.set.poly(scmp_ob, poly_degree = 2)
scmp_ob <- sc.p.vector(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
scmp_ob <- sc.t.fit(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
scmp_ob <- sc.filter(scmp_ob, rsq = 0.7, vars = "groups")
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(res))]))
```

# From a trajectory graph

Tools that describe a trajectory as a graph, such as the principal graph of
Monocle3 or a minimum spanning tree of clusters, give every cell a node of
the graph. `paths_from_graph()` turns the graph into lineage weights: each
lineage is the path from the root node to an end node, and a cell has
weight 1 on the lineages that pass through its node and 0 elsewhere. It
finds the paths with the igraph package [@csardi2006].

The graph here has the Monocle3 path labels of `multi.lin.sce` as its nodes:
the root joins the end path `path_Y_52` and the link, and the link joins the
other two end paths.

```{r graph}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)
edges <- rbind(
    c("root", "path_Y_52"),
    c("root", "path_Y_18|path_Y_15"),
    c("path_Y_18|path_Y_15", "path_Y_15"),
    c("path_Y_18|path_Y_15", "path_Y_18")
)
cell_node <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$group
names(cell_node) <- colnames(multi.lin.sce)
graph_weights <- paths_from_graph(cell_node, edges, root = "root")
head(graph_weights)
```

The end nodes are the nodes with one edge other than the root, in the order
in which they appear in `edges`; `endpoints` chooses them. With the Monocle3
pseudotime, shared by every lineage, `assign_paths()` gives back the path
labels of the data set, with the link written in the `_links_` format:

```{r graph-paths}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)
graph_cells <- assign_paths(
    colData(multi.lin.sce)$Monocle3_Pseudotime, graph_weights
)
table(graph_cells$Path)
```

# From Monocle3

A Monocle3 `cell_data_set` after `learn_graph()` and `order_cells()` holds
the same pieces: the principal graph, the nearest node of each cell, the
root node and the pseudotime. The code below builds the cell table from
them with `paths_from_graph()` and `assign_paths()`. It is not run here:
monocle3 is distributed on GitHub, not on CRAN or Bioconductor, so
scMaSigPro cannot depend on it.

```{r monocle3, eval = FALSE}
library(monocle3)
# `cds`: a cell_data_set after learn_graph() and order_cells()
graph <- principal_graph(cds)[["UMAP"]]
aux <- principal_graph_aux(cds)[["UMAP"]]

# The nearest node of each cell, as a node name, and the root node
nearest <- aux$pr_graph_cell_proj_closest_vertex
cell_node <- igraph::V(graph)$name[nearest[, 1]]
names(cell_node) <- rownames(nearest)
root <- aux$root_pr_nodes

# One lineage per end node, then the path label of each cell
weights <- paths_from_graph(cell_node, igraph::as_edgelist(graph),
    root = root
)
cells <- assign_paths(pseudotime(cds), weights)

scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(cds)[, rownames(cells)],
    cell_data = cells,
    ptime_col = "Pseudotime",
    path_col = "Path"
)
```

The principal graph often has more end nodes than the branches of
interest, and a graph learnt on several partitions has parts that the root
cannot reach; `endpoints` names the end nodes of the lineages to analyse,
which must be reachable from the root. Cells on none of these lineages, and
cells with an infinite pseudotime, are left out.

# Other tools

Any tool will do that gives a pseudotime and a lineage for every cell. With
lineage weights, as slingshot and tradeSeq give them, `assign_paths()` makes
the labels; with a graph of nodes, `paths_from_graph()` makes the weights
first. With hard labels already, as `multi.lin.sce` has them, add the two
columns to the `colData()` and call `as_scmp()`, or pass the table to
`create_scmp()`.
